docs.text: ** Team 207 | Aziyah Castellanoz Subsystem:** Temperature & Humidity Sensing Transmission

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The purpose of this block diagram is to define the electrical design, signal flow, power distribution, and the board interface connections for the Temperature & Humidity Sensing Transmission Subsystem.

This diagram documents how major integrated circuits, digital signal connection, and user interface peripherals connect to the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano microcontroller, as well as how data and digital signals pass to the main board thorough the team's 8-pin connector.

docs.title: Key Architectural Elements
docs.text:
Power Sources and Voltage * External Power Input: 12V DC wall adapter entering through a PCB barrel jack which is protected by a inline fuse. * Regulated Logic Rail(5V DC): L7805ABV-DG 1.5A linear regulator with input(0.33uf) and output(0.1uf) filtering capacitors. * Ground Common system Earth Ground rail shared across all block and team interfaces.

Sensor Subsystem: * DHT20 Temperature and Humidity Sensor Communicates with PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano via a two wire I2C serial protocol. * Op-Amp Buffer Stage: Using the MCP6004 the DHT11 will pass through the op-amp to prevent signal degradation and input loading.

User Interface and Debugging Indicators: * Pushbuttons: Active user input switches tied to RA4 and RA3 with 10k pull up resistors. * Debug Status LED: General purpose visual status indicator on pin RA0 with a 300 ohm current limiting resistor. * Spare GPIO Expansion Header: 1x6 male header that has power, ground, and 4 unused GPIO pins for testing or probing.

Team Inter-Board Connections(8-pin Header): * Pin 1 ('DigitalSignal2'): Digital control line routed to PIC pin RA3. * Pin 2 ('DigitalSignal1'): Digital control line routed to PIC pin RA4. * Pin 3 ('UART_TX'): UART serial data output from PIC transmitting sensor data packets to main board. * Pin 4 ('UART_RX'): UART serial data input to PIC receiving commands from the main board. * Pin 5-7 ('DigitalSignal2'): Reserved pass-through lines for team expansion * Pin 8 ('Earth' Ground): Class stnadard common ground return line

docs.title: Component Selection for Design
docs.text:
Tempature & Humidity Sensing Transmission

**Component 1: Temperature & Humidity Sensor ** Pros Cons Option 1. 1188-SNS-DHT11-ND$3.95/eachlink to product * high humidity range* Only needs one GPIO pin * Compact for small project design * Lower accuracy* Maximum sampling rate 1HZ * Option 2. * CANADUINO 26085 * $2.39/each * Link to product * Cheaper than other options * Wide voltage range * 16 bit output provides high resolution data * Low relative humidity(RH) limit * lower quality DHT11 * Option 3. * 1188-SNS-DHT22-ND * $7.30/each * Link to product *High precision * Fast response time * Industry Standard * Expensive * Harder to hand solder * Require external pull-up resistors * Option 4. * DHT20 - AHT20 * $4.50/each * Link to product * Fast response time with 8 seconds * High temperature and humidity accuracy * Wide voltage range from 2.2V to 5.0V * Requires 2 GPIO pins * Requires bus pull up resistors and Decoupling capacitors * Manuel soldering constraints

Choice: Option 4: DHT20 - AHT20 PIN MODULE - I2C T

Rationale: The DHT20 temperature and humidity sensor created by Adafruit was selected to replace my initial selection of the DHT11 to fully comply with the EGR304 course guidelines while upgrading the overall system performance. The DHT20 comes as a standalone 4-pin through hole component that can be soldered directly onto our custom PCB boards as well transitions the subsystem communication to a standard I^2C which is more reliable and compatible with our PIC18F57Q43's hardware. Compared to the original DHT11, the DHT20 has a superior relative humidity and temperature accuracy and has a lower cost.

**Component 2: 5v Linear Voltage Regulator ** Pros Cons Option 1. L7805ABV-DG$1.53/eachlink to product * High output accuracy* Wide operating temperature * Stable over a wide input voltage range * Gets hot too quickly * Requires a minimum of 2v dropout voltage * Option 2. * MC7805CTGOS-ND$1.01/each * Link to product * Low dropout voltage * Built in heatsink * High current capability * Poor power efficiency * Maximum output current limited to 250 mA * Consumes a operating current of 5mA to 6.5mA * Option 3. * MCP1700-5002E/TO-ND * $0.50/each * Link to product *Extremely inexpensive * Very low operating current(µA) * Built in circuit protection * Narrow input voltage margin * Requires input/output filter capacitors for stability

Choice: Option 1: L7805ABV-DG

Rationale: The L7805ABV-DG was selected due to its capability of sourcing a 1.5A max output current which will provide a safe current for our design and its built in circuit protection incase of a short circuit. It is also a standard stock component, even being used in some of the in class Lab, also providing thermal protection feature such as a heatsink to reduce heat with high voltage.

**Component 3: External Power Supply ** Pros Cons Option 1.993-PSAC05R-050L6-R-ND$5.56/eachlink to product * high efficiency * Reliable output * Interchangeable AC plugs * AC plugs sold separately* Limited to 5 watts * Option 2. * 839-16-00078-ND * $7.51/each * Link to product * Wide input range * Standard output connector * High energy efficiecy * Low power output * Low operating tempature * Option 3. * WSU120-0700 * $7.58/each * Link to product *Clean and regulated output * Long cord length * Affordable * Narrow operating temperature

Choice: Option 3: WSU120-0700 AC/DC WALL MNT ADAPTER 12V 8.4W

Rationale: The WSU120-0700 was chosen since it satisfies the regulator dropout requirements, for example our chosen voltage regulator requires a minimum of 7 volts which our 12V DC output satisfies. The 700 mA at 12v DC provides significant current headroom to pass the 25 percent current safety margin, it also has a integrated barrel plug that is compatible with the barrel jack on our PCB.

Overview
docs.text:
This subsystem schematic integrates power regulation, digital processing, environmental sensing, inter-board serial communication, user interface controls via push buttons, and expansion test points into a single PCB design. The system will operate on a +12 volt DC input from a wall plug which is fused and regulated down to +5 volt DC to power the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano microcontroller, the DHT20 temperature and humidity sensor, and all other peripherals.

Figure 01: Showing Temperature Sensor Schematic.
